ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows the square cross-section of the cubical Gaussian surface in the x-y plane, bounded symmetrically about the origin. A charged disk is centered on the left face of the cube, so only its right half lies inside the cube. A charged rod lies on the positive x-axis, beginning inside the cube and extending outside through the right face. One point charge is inside the square region and another is outside it. Reasoning: The cube is the region -a/2 <= x <= a/2, -a/2 <= y <= a/2, -a/2 <= z <= a/2. By Gauss's law, the electric flux through the closed cubical surface is Q_enclosed/ε0. The disk has total charge 6C and is centered at (-a/2, 0, 0) with radius a/4 in the x-y plane. The plane x = -a/2 cuts the disk through its center, so only half of the uniformly charged disk is inside the cube: enclosed disk charge = 6C/2 = 3C. The rod has total charge 8C over length a, from x = a/4 to x = 5a/4. Inside the cube it extends only from x = a/4 to x = a/2, a length a/4, which is one-fourth of the rod, so enclosed rod charge = 8C * 1/4 = 2C. The point charge -7C at (a/4, -a/4, 0) lies within all coordinate bounds, so it is enclosed. The point charge +3C at (-3a/4, 3a/4, 0) is outside the cube, so it is not enclosed. Therefore Q_enclosed = 3C + 2C - 7C = -2C. Hence the flux is -2C/ε0.

A charged rod lies on the positive x-axis, beginning inside the cube and extending outside through the right face. One point charge is inside the square region and another is outside it.

Reasoning: The cube is the region -a/2 <= x <= a/2, -a/2 <= y <= a/2, -a/2 <= z <= a/2. By Gauss's law, the electric flux through the closed cubical surface is Q_enclosed/ε0. The disk has total charge 6C and is centered at (-a/2, 0, 0) with radius a/4 in the x-y plane. The plane x = -a/2 cuts the disk through its center, so only half of the uniformly charged disk is inside the cube: enclosed disk charge = 6C/2 = 3C. The rod has total charge 8C over length a, from x = a/4 to x = 5a/4. Inside the cube it extends only from x = a/4 to x = a/2, a length a/4, which is one-fourth of the rod, so enclosed rod charge = 8C * 1/4 = 2C. The point charge -7C at (a/4, -a/4, 0) lies within all coordinate bounds, so it is enclosed. The point charge +3C at (-3a/4, 3a/4, 0) is outside the cube, so it is not enclosed. Therefore Q_enclosed = 3C + 2C - 7C = -2C. Hence the flux is -2C/ε0.
